situation.note: twenty two years in one company and they let me go in a 10 minute call. I have not told my mother. Every morning I still wake up at 6 like I have to go to office.

understanding.bridge: The ten minute call that ended twenty two years is what the Gita calls a result that was never yours to hold. Your worth is not the one they took away.
understanding.core_struggle: After twenty two years at one company, was let go in a ten minute call and is hiding it from their mother, waking each morning as if they still had to go.
understanding.mirror: You gave them twenty two years, and they took it back in ten minutes.
understanding.insight: You have not told your mother, and that silence is its own weight. The morning routine is what the body does when the mind has not yet caught up.

queries.hook: Being let go after twenty two years in a call that lasted ten minutes, and the hollow morning that follows when the office no longer exists. I lost a parent.
queries.diagnose: When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth, and the harm deepens when we hide it.
queries.steady: A failure is something that happened, not who you are; no one who has served with honesty is ever lost, and no one can take away what you have already built.
queries.act: Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; learn what this taught you, make amends where you can, and begin again.
queries.story: A man of long service who was dismissed and hid the loss from his own family, yet found the courage to stand again and offer what he had to offer.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verse.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
verse.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.for_you: Love does not end when a life does; grieve fully, and let the bond keep living in how you live.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama, near the end of his lament, says where the real enemy lives.
verse.sanskrit: शत्रवश्चेन्द्रियाण्येव सत्यं यातमसत्यताम् । प्रहरत्यात्मनैवात्मा मनसैव मनो रिपुः ॥
verse.line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
verse.translation: Our own senses are the enemies; truth itself has turned untrue; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to blame yourself. Vasishtha's answer is that the same mind can lift itself.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.for_you: The self in the one you love and the self in you were never born and never pass away; love was a meeting of what lasts.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Closing verse of the section on steadfastness.
verse.sanskrit: छिन्नोऽपि रोहति तरुश्चन्द्रः क्षीणोऽपि वर्धते लोके । इति विमृशन्तः सन्तः सन्तप्यन्ते न लोकेऽस्मिन् ॥
verse.line: A cut tree grows back; the waning moon fills again. Remembering this, the wise do not despair.
verse.translation: A tree that is cut grows again; the waning moon waxes again in the world. Reflecting on this, the good are not tormented in this world.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari closes his section on steadfastness with an image of nature's patience. He tells the reader that a tree cut down will grow back, and the moon that wanes will wax again. The point is simple. Hard times in themselves do not destroy a person who keeps walking the right path. The setback is real, but it is not the final word.
verse.for_you: You are still the person who arrived at the office at six every morning for two decades.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing at work that is still in your hands today.
verse.scene_line: You are a cut tree still standing in your own yard.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verse.line: Whatever is born will die, and what dies is born again. Don't torment yourself over the unavoidable.
verse.translation: Death is certain for the one who is born, and birth is certain for the one who dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to stop caring for the sick or to rush someone's mourning.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield of as Arjuna lays down his bow, refusing to fight his own kin. Krishna tells him that the soul is eternal, wearing bodies as one discards old clothes. What comes into being will pass away, and what passes will come into being again. He asks Arjuna not to grieve for what is unavoidable, for the true self is never born and never dies.
verse.for_you: The ten minute call ended a chapter, but it did not end you. The body still wakes at six and walks to the office because it has not yet heard that the ground has shifted. You are the one who remains.
verse.try_today: Let the mind rest from the call for one hour.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of the battlefield, still holding the bow.
asks: How do I tell my mother what happened?
Can I still be the same person at work?
What part of me is still here?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the self is both its own greatest friend and its own worst enemy. The mind can lift itself up, or it can sink itself down with blame and doubt. You are not helpless against this. The choice to be kind to yourself is entirely yours.
verse.for_you: Let yourself grieve, honour them by living well, and remember that the self they loved in you, and in them, does not perish.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you speak to yourself with patience instead of blame.
asks: How do I stop being my own worst enemy?
What does it mean to be my own friend?
Can I lift myself up without pretending?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
verse.sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
verse.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
verse.translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
verse.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to Bharat, who is shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile. Bharat hears the call to rule but knows his heart will not accept it without Ram. So he decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive. The verse says that when the head and heart are at war, you could go and face the person you think you wronged.
verse.for_you: Your own silence is its own weight, and it sits in your chest like a stone.
verse.try_today: Walk to the place where you keep the truth hidden.
verse.scene_line: You are standing at the door of a room you have not entered.
asks: How do I begin to face what I have hidden?
What does facing myself look like right now?
What is the first step I can take?

story.title: Ram accepts exile
story.story_hook: He went to the palace to be crowned and came out with fourteen years in the forest.
story.summary: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.
story.lesson: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.

matched.label: I have to give someone bad news

anchor.speaker: Narrator
anchor.setting: Ram walks out of the palace, having lost the throne he was to receive that morning.
anchor.sanskrit: न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्। सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥
anchor.line: He had just lost the kingdom, and his mind showed no change at all.
anchor.translation: As he set out for the forest and gave up the earth, no change could be seen in his mind, as if he stood beyond the world.
anchor.why: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.
anchor.misuse: Calm in loss is not pretending it does not hurt; Ram grieves elsewhere in the story.

prasang.title: Ram accepts exile
prasang.summary: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.
prasang.story_hook: He went to the palace to be crowned and came out with fourteen years in the forest.
prasang.lesson: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.

story.hook_title: Ram went to be crowned and came out exiled for fourteen years
story.teaser: Ram went to be crowned and came out exiled for fourteen years
story.for_you: Ram walks out of the palace with the kingdom gone, and his mind shows no change yet. You wake at six and go to a place that no longer holds your name, and the body moves because it does not know the call has ended.
asks: How do I stop the morning routine from feeling like a lie?
Can I be my own friend when I feel so hollowed out?
